On August 5, 2026, Gran Tierra entered into a definitive Share Sale and Purchase Agreement (the “Share Purchase Agreement”) to sell its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses (the “Sale”) to Maurel & Prom for total consideration of approximately $1.33 billion, subject to adjustment, including the assumption of its 2031 Notes, its 9.50% Senior Secured Amortizing Notes due 2029 and the facility under its oil prepayment agreement.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Gran Tierra repurchased $24.2 million in face value of the Company’s 9.75% Senior Secured Amortizing Notes due 2031 (the “2031 Notes”) at a discount of 11% to the face value of the repurchased 2031 Notes.

financial_health.claim: Gran Tierra intends to meet and eliminate its debt through the Maurel & Prom sale for approximately $1.33 billion in total consideration—under which the buyer assumes the 2029 Notes, 2031 Notes, and oil prepayment agreement facility—and expects approximately $315 million in net cash proceeds ($250 million in cash including the $50 million deposit, plus $65 million under an unsecured note due 364 days after closing) and to be debt-free on closing.
quotes: On August 5, 2026, Gran Tierra entered into a definitive Share Sale and Purchase Agreement (the “Share Purchase Agreement”) to sell its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses (the “Sale”) to Maurel & Prom for total consideration of approximately $1.33 billion, subject to adjustment, including the assumption of its 2031 Notes, its 9.50% Senior Secured Amortizing Notes due 2029 and the facility under its oil prepayment agreement.
Expected net cash proceeds are approximately $315 million.

Of the expected net cash proceeds, approximately $250 million is payable in cash, including the $50 million deposit received during the Quarter, which is included in the $141 million cash balance, and the remaining $65 million is payable under an unsecured note 364 days after closing.
On closing, we expect to be debt-free, with the flexibility to return capital to stockholders and build our businesses in Canada and Azerbaijan.

financial_health.claim: Although Gran Tierra secured 2031 Note holder consent on September 22, 2026 and stockholder approval on October 9, 2026 and targets closing before year-end, completion remains subject to regulatory approvals in Colombia and Ecuador and termination rights including on a material adverse change, leaving $141 million in cash and approximately $53 million in undrawn Canadian credit facility availability as the stated liquidity cushion.
quotes: On September 22, 2026, following receipt of the requisite consents from holders of the 2031 Notes, the Company executed a supplemental indenture in connection with the Sale, which becomes operative on closing.
On October 9, 2026, Gran Tierra’s stockholders approved the Sale.
Closing remains subject to the remaining consents, regulatory approvals in Colombia and Ecuador and other closing conditions, and the Company continues to target closing before the end of the year.
The completion of the Sale is subject to a number of conditions, certain of which are outside of control of Gran Tierra and Purchaser, including certain regulatory approvals in Colombia and Ecuador.
For instance, Purchaser has the right, in certain circumstances, to terminate the Share Purchase Agreement following delivery of a notice regarding the occurrence of a material adverse change.
In addition to the $141 million cash on hand as of September 30, 2026, the Company has approximately $53 million in undrawn availability under its Canadian revolving credit facility.
